headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.1879). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.71 (95% CI: 0.55–0.94), suggesting that garlic is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer. These findings were supported by moderate between-study heterogeneity (I² = 44.18%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.
